### shard_reflect.h

Interface `"shard.reflect"` 1.0 : what exists in the engine and in the other plugins, described at run time ; and functions plugins offer to be called by name.

A tool that does not know the game when it is written needs this : a visual scripting editor lists the components, their fields, the events and the functions it can wire together, a UI binds a label to `"Health.current"` of an actor, a console completes names, a network layer walks the fields of a component to send them. The engine's own components (`"light"`, `"model"`...), the components and scripts of every C plugin, the events described with `shard.events`' `describe` and the functions below are all listed through the same calls.

A FUNCTION is a named piece of code with a typed signature : `"nav.set_destination(actor, vec3) -> bool"`. A plugin registers the ones it wants a graph, a UI binding or a console to call ; anything with a signature that fits is called through `function_call` with `ShardValues`. They are not a way for plugins to call each other in hot code (`shard.services` is) : a call converts its arguments to `ShardValue` and back.

Names live in one flat space. A plugin prefixes its own with its id or a short name of its choice (`"nav.set_destination"`) ; a function another plugin already registered under that name is `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS`.

thread : main, except where a function says otherwise.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_REFLECT` | `"shard.reflect"` |  |

The types a value has. Fields of the engine's components are described with these too (more than `shard.components`' `SHARD_FIELD_*` can say).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_VALUE_NONE` | `0u` |  |
| `SHARD_VALUE_BOOL` | `1u` | `ShardValue::i` is 0 or 1 |
| `SHARD_VALUE_I32` | `2u` | i |
| `SHARD_VALUE_I64` | `3u` | i |
| `SHARD_VALUE_F32` | `4u` | f[0] |
| `SHARD_VALUE_F64` | `5u` | d |
| `SHARD_VALUE_VEC2` | `6u` | f[0..1] |
| `SHARD_VALUE_VEC3` | `7u` | f[0..2] |
| `SHARD_VALUE_VEC4` | `8u` | f[0..3] |
| `SHARD_VALUE_QUAT` | `9u` | f[0..3] : x, y, z, w |
| `SHARD_VALUE_COLOR` | `10u` | f[0..3] : r, g, b, a |
| `SHARD_VALUE_STRING` | `11u` | s : UTF-8 |
| `SHARD_VALUE_ACTOR` | `12u` | i : a `ShardActor` |
| `SHARD_VALUE_ASSET` | `13u` | i : an asset id (`shard.assets`), 0 for none |
| `SHARD_VALUE_JSON` | `14u` | s : any value as JSON text (a list, a struct, what has no type of its own) |
| `SHARD_VALUE_ENUM` | `15u` | s : the name of the chosen value |
| `SHARD_VALUE_ANY` | `16u` | a parameter that takes any of the above (a `"print"` node) ; a value itself never has this type |

#### ShardValue

One value, flat so that its layout is plain. Which members are used is said above ; the others are ignored on input and zero on output. A string is valid for the call it is passed to or returned from, and for a returned value until the same function is called again on this thread.

```c
uint32_t type;    // SHARD_VALUE_*
uint32_t reserved;
int64_t i;
double d;
float f[4];
ShardStr s;
```

**Types**

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_TYPE_COMPONENT` | `1u` | a component of an actor : the engine's (`"light"`), or a plugin's (`"com.acme.Spin"`, a script too) |
| `SHARD_TYPE_EVENT` | `2u` | an event by name, with the payload `shard.events`' `describe` gave it |

#### ShardTypeInfo

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t kind;    // SHARD_TYPE_*
uint32_t fieldCount;
uint32_t flags;    // SHARD_TYPE_FLAG_*
ShardStr name;    // valid while the type is registered
```

Runs the function. `args` has `argCount` values (never fewer than the required parameters) ; fill `results`, which has `resultCount` zeroed values, and return `SHARD_OK`, or an error (`SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` for a value the function cannot take). thread : the caller's.


**Types**

How many types of that kind (`SHARD_TYPE_*`) there are now, and the one at an index (stable while no plugin is loaded or unloaded). The caller sets out-&gt;structSize. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : the index is out of range. thread : main

```c

ShardResult type_at(uint32_t kind, uint32_t index, ShardTypeInfo* out);
```

A type by its name (`"light"`, `"com.acme.Spin"`, `"com.acme.RainStarted"`). `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND`.

```c
ShardResult type_find(uint32_t kind, ShardStr name, ShardTypeInfo* out);
```

The fields of a type, in the order the inspector shows them. For an event : the fields `describe` gave.

```c

```

The names a `SHARD_VALUE_ENUM` field takes, by index.

```c

```

**Functions**

Registers a function, from `on_load` or later. It goes with the plugin. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : a bad name, a callback missing, an optional parameter before a required one.

```c
ShardResult function_add(ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardFunctionDesc* desc);
ShardResult function_remove(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name);
uint32_t function_count(void);
ShardResult function_at(uint32_t index, ShardFunctionInfo* out);
ShardResult function_find(ShardStr name, ShardFunctionInfo* out);
```

A parameter (result == `SHARD_FALSE`) or a result (`SHARD_TRUE`) of a function, by index.

```c
ShardResult function_param_at(ShardStr name, int32_t result, uint32_t index, ShardParamDesc* out);
```

Calls it. The arguments are checked against the signature (a missing optional one is left out, a number is converted to the type asked, anything else is `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG`) ; `results` receives resultCount values. thread : the one the function is made for -- script or main (the host answers `SHARD_E_WRONG_THREAD` otherwise), and not from a job.

```c
ShardResult function_call(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, const ShardValue* args, uint32_t arg_count, ShardValue* results, uint32_t result_count);
```

### shard_render.h

Interface `"shard.render"` 1.0 : what a plugin puts on the screen that the engine's components do not : meshes it builds, textures it fills, sprites, instances and a 2D overlay.

The engine draws from a snapshot of the simulation (Extract stage), not from the world, and so does this : a plugin hands the renderer RESOURCES (a mesh, a texture, a material), and RETAINED things that use them (a render object, a batch of sprites, an overlay), which the host copies into each frame's snapshot. Nothing here draws `"now"` : a call records, the frame draws. The GPU work happens on the render thread ; the plugin never waits for it, and a handle can be used at once even if its upload is not done (what is not uploaded yet is not drawn).

```
- voxels      : a Mesh per chunk (mesh_create from a job), a RenderObject per chunk, a texture array for the atlas
- particles   : a SpriteBatch (sprite_batch_set every frame from a system), or an InstanceBatch of meshes
- animation   : a skinned Mesh (JOINTS + WEIGHTS) and object_set_pose with the bone matrices every frame
```

* runtime UI  : an Overlay (a callback that draws the UI's geometry into the frame), Geometry and Textures for what it draws, and
```
an Overlay on a render-target Texture to put a UI on a surface of the world
```

* navigation, AI, networking : `shard.debug` draws their debug views

Handles are 64 bit, owned by the plugin, 0 is never valid, and all of them are released with the plugin (disable or unload). Positions in the world are the ABI's usual ones (`shard_actors.h`) ; a large world's positions are doubles. Matrices are 16 floats, column major (x axis first). Colours are 8 bit r, g, b, a packed as r \| g &lt;&lt; 8 \| b &lt;&lt; 16 \| a &lt;&lt; 24, straight (not premultiplied) alpha.

thread : any, for the functions that create, update or destroy a resource or a retained thing (they take a lock and record). thread : main for `load_*`, the camera and the overlay's callback. A host without a renderer (a server, a tool, the tests) accepts every call, keeps the handles and draws nothing : `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` only for the functions that read the screen back (`camera_info`, `world_to_screen`...).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_RENDER` | `"shard.render"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardMesh;
typedef uint64_t ShardTexture;
typedef uint64_t ShardMaterial;
typedef uint64_t ShardRenderObject;
typedef uint64_t ShardSpriteBatch;
typedef uint64_t ShardInstanceBatch;
typedef uint64_t ShardGeometry;
typedef uint64_t ShardOverlay;
```

**Meshes**

Vertex attributes, in the order they are laid out in a vertex (interleaved, no padding). POSITION is always there.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_VERTEX_POSITION` | `0x01u` | float x3 |
| `SHARD_VERTEX_NORMAL` | `0x02u` | float x3 |
| `SHARD_VERTEX_TANGENT` | `0x04u` | float x4 : xyz and the handedness in w |
| `SHARD_VERTEX_UV0` | `0x08u` | float x2 |
| `SHARD_VERTEX_UV1` | `0x10u` | float x2 : the lightmap's coordinates, or a second texture's |
| `SHARD_VERTEX_COLOR` | `0x20u` | uint8 x4, normalised |
| `SHARD_VERTEX_JOINTS` | `0x40u` | uint16 x4 : the bones this vertex follows (skinning) |
| `SHARD_VERTEX_WEIGHTS` | `0x80u` | float x4 : how much each of them, summing to 1 (skinning) |
| `SHARD_MESH_INDEX16` | `1u` | the indices are `uint16_t`, not `uint32_t` |
| `SHARD_MESH_DYNAMIC` | `2u` | updated often (every frame, or nearly) : the host picks storage that suits |

**The 2D overlay**

#### ShardVertex2D

The vertex of 2D geometry : the layout of a UI library's vertices (RmlUi, Dear ImGui's draw lists...). position is in pixels of the target, from its top left corner ; the colour multiplies the texture.

```c
float position[2];
uint32_t color;
float uv[2];
```

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_CLIP_DISABLE` | `0u` | no mask : what follows is not clipped by one |
| `SHARD_CLIP_SET` | `1u` | the mask becomes the geometry's area |
| `SHARD_CLIP_SET_INVERSE` | `2u` | the mask becomes everything but the geometry's area |
| `SHARD_CLIP_INTERSECT` | `3u` | the mask is cut down to the geometry's area |

#### ShardDrawApi

What the overlay's callback draws with : records commands into the frame. Valid during the callback only. The commands draw in the order they were given, over what the 3D scene drew (and over earlier overlays).

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Draws a geometry, moved by `translation` pixels, with `texture` (0 : plain colour). The blending is PREMULTIPLIED alpha (source \* 1 + destination

* (1 - source alpha)) : the colours of the vertices and the texels of the textures are expected premultiplied, as a UI library such as RmlUi

produces them. A `texture_load` image is straight alpha : premultiply it, or load it yourself and use `texture_create`.

```c
void draw_geometry(ShardGeometry geometry, ShardTexture texture, const float translation[2]);
```

The transform applied to what follows, 16 floats column major, in pixels ; NULL : none.

```c
void set_transform(const float matrix[16]);
```

The rectangle (x, y from the top left, width, height, in pixels) nothing is drawn outside of, while `enabled`.

```c
void set_scissor(int32_t enabled, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t width, int32_t height);
```

A mask by shape (`SHARD_CLIP_*`) : what follows is drawn only inside the area the geometry covers (rounded corners, rotated clips). A host without a stencil buffer (this one, for the viewport) clips to the bounding rectangle of the shape, and `SHARD_CLIP_SET_INVERSE` does not clip.

```c
void set_clip_mask(uint32_t operation, ShardGeometry geometry, const float translation[2]);
```

Fills the target with a colour (r, g, b, a floats in 0..1) : the first thing an overlay on a render-target texture does.

```c
void clear(const float rgba[4]);
```

Geometry for this frame only (a debug overlay, a one-off quad) : copied, no handle to manage.

```c
void draw_triangles(const ShardVertex2D* vertices, uint32_t vertexCount, const uint32_t* indices, uint32_t indexCount, ShardTexture texture);
```

#### ShardOverlayFrame

What an overlay is told when it is asked to draw

```c

float dpiScale;    // 1 on a normal display, 2 on a "retina" one...

```

thread : main. Called once per frame for each overlay, after the simulation, before the frame is handed to the renderer.

Geometry the overlay draws again and again (a UI library compiles its elements once). Copied. thread : any

```c
ShardResult geometry_create(ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardVertex2D* vertices, uint32_t vertexCount, const uint32_t* indices, uint32_t indexCount, ShardGeometry* out);
ShardResult geometry_destroy(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardGeometry geometry);
```

**The camera**

The active camera of the game's viewport. The caller sets out-&gt;structSize. thread : main or script. `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : no renderer.

```c
ShardResult camera_info(ShardCameraInfo* out);
```

A point of the world as the camera sees it : x, y in pixels of the viewport from its top left, z the distance along the view axis (negative : behind the camera).

```c
ShardResult world_to_screen(const double position[3], float out[3]);
```

The ray through a pixel of the viewport : an origin in the world and a unit direction.

```c
ShardResult screen_to_ray(float x, float y, double origin[3], float direction[3]);
```

### shard_scripts.h

Interface `"shard.scripts"` 1.2 : scripts, the components that carry a plugin's gameplay code.

A script is an object of the plugin (a C++ class in the SDK) that lives on an actor, as the engine's own Script components do. The host owns its memory and calls it back : it is created with the component, receives the callbacks of the actor's life and of the frame (play, tick, fixed tick, late tick, stop...), in the order of the scripts of the world, and goes with the actor. Its fields are shown by the inspector, saved with the world and copied with the actor (play mode copies the world), exactly as for a component of `shard_components.h` : the same `ShardFieldDesc`, the same field types (text, assets, blobs included), at offsets in the object.

Unlike a component's block, the object is NOT plain data : it is constructed in place in storage the host provides (`size` bytes, aligned on `align`), and destructed there. It is never moved or copied by the host with memcpy. A copy of the actor (play mode) constructs a new object and copies the described fields into it : what is not a field starts fresh, as if the actor was just created.

Threads : every callback runs on the thread that ticks the scripts of the world, one script after the other, never two at once : what a script does with `shard_actors.h` and `shard_input.h` is safe there. The functions of this table are `"thread : main"` (from `on_load`).

Edit mode (1.2) : the engine ticks scripts only while the world plays (`on_create` does run when a script joins an actor in the editor, `on_play` only in play mode). A script that has to be seen working while it is being made -- a particle emitter, a UI being laid out, an animation being scrubbed, a navigation mesh being tuned -- sets `SHARD_SCRIPT_EDIT_MODE` in its description : `on_edit_tick` is then called every frame the world does NOT play (with the real frame time). `on_field_changed` is called when the inspector edits one of a script's fields, in either mode. What a script does in edit mode must not change what gets saved: the world file holds the fields, not the state of an effect.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_SCRIPTS` | `"shard.scripts"` |  |
| `SHARD_SCRIPT_MAX_SIZE` | `16384u` | bytes of an object |

The callbacks of a script. All are optional but construct and destruct. A callback returns `SHARD_OK`, or an error that the host logs and counts as an error of the plugin (at the tenth the host fails the plugin, as for a system). `object` is what construct built.

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardScriptFn)(void* user, void* object);
typedef ShardResult (*ShardScriptTickFn)(void* user, void* object, float delta_time);
```

#### ShardContact

What a script is told about a contact of its actor's body with another one (physics, ABI 1.5). `other` is the other body's actor. `normal` points from this actor toward the other one. `point` is a point of the contact in the world, `penetration` how deep the bodies overlap. `on_contact_ended` only fills `other`.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
ShardActor other;
float point[3];
float normal[3];
float penetration;
```

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardScriptContactFn)(void* user, void* object, const ShardContact* contact);
```

#### ShardScriptCallbacks

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Builds the object in `storage` : fields at their defaults, no actor yet. Called when the component is made (an actor getting it, the world file read, a copy of an actor). `SHARD_OK`, or an error to refuse (the component is not made).

```c
ShardResult construct(void* user, void* storage);
```

Destroys the object. The storage is the host's to free.

```c
void destruct(void* user, void* storage);
```

The component joined an actor : this is its owner, valid as long as the object lives. Called once, before `on_create`.

```c
ShardResult attach(void* user, void* object, ShardActor owner);
ShardScriptFn on_create;    // the script joined an actor that is in a world (Script::OnCreate)
ShardScriptFn on_world_loaded;    // the world finished loading (for actors tagged "Persistent")
ShardScriptFn on_world_unloaded;
ShardScriptFn on_play;    // play mode starts
ShardScriptTickFn on_tick;    // every frame, in the Update phase : delta_time is the frame's
ShardScriptTickFn on_fixed_tick;    // every fixed step, right before the physics step : delta_time is the step's
ShardScriptTickFn on_late_tick;    // every frame, after the scripts and the physics moved everything
ShardScriptFn on_stop;    // play mode stops
ShardScriptFn on_destroyed;    // the component or its actor is destroyed, before destruct
ShardScriptFn on_activated;
ShardScriptFn on_deactivated;
```

1.5 : physics contacts, in the physics step's callbacks, on the thread that steps the physics

```c
ShardScriptContactFn on_contact_added;
ShardScriptContactFn on_contact_persisted;
ShardScriptContactFn on_contact_ended;
```

1.5 : the plugin's own strings. A field `SHARD_FIELD_STRING` with `SHARD_FIELD_ACCESSOR` is the object's `std::string` (or any string of the plugin's) at that offset : the host never reads its memory, it asks these. `text_get` gives the text (valid until the next call into the object), `text_set` replaces it. Both are required when a field has the flag.

```c
void text_get(void* user, void* object, uint32_t offset, ShardStr* out);
ShardResult text_set(void* user, void* object, uint32_t offset, ShardStr text);
```

**1.2**

```c
ShardScriptTickFn on_edit_tick;    // SHARD_SCRIPT_EDIT_MODE : every frame while the world does not play
```

A field was edited (inspector, `shard.actors`' `set_component`, an undo) ; `field` is its index in the description's `fields`. Not called for the fields the script changes itself.

```c
ShardResult on_field_changed(void* user, void* object, uint32_t field);
```

Callbacks of later ABI revisions go HERE : the host checks structSize before reading them.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_SCRIPT_EDIT_MODE` | `1u` | `ShardScriptDesc::flags` : also run in the editor's edit mode, see above |

#### ShardScriptDesc

```c
uint32_t structSize;

uint32_t align;    // a power of two, 16 at most
uint32_t fieldCount;    // SHARD_COMPONENT_MAX_FIELDS at most
ShardStr name;    // "Health" : the host registers "<plugin id>.Health", the name a world file calls it
const ShardFieldDesc* fields;    // offsets in the object. Read during the call only.
void* user;    // handed back to every callback
const ShardScriptCallbacks* callbacks;    // copied up to its structSize during the call
```

**1.2**

```c

uint32_t reserved;
```

#### ShardScriptsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Registers a script type, from `on_load`. thread : main. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : a field out of the object, misaligned or overlapping another, a bad name, a size or an alignment out of bounds, no construct or destruct (the log says which). `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : the name is taken.

```c
ShardResult register_script(ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardScriptDesc* desc);
```

The object of the script `name` (as registered, `"Health"`) that `actor` has, if it belongs to this plugin : NULL in `*out` otherwise. Valid until the script is removed or the actor destroyed. thread : script

```c

```

### shard_time.h

Interface `"shard.time"` 1.0 : the simulation's clock, and a fingerprint of its state.

A system or a script is handed the step it runs for (`shard_systems.h`, `shard_scripts.h`) ; this is for the rest : a particle emitter that wants the simulation time to seed its randomness, a network layer that numbers its ticks, a UI that animates in real time.

Two kinds of time. The simulation's (`simTime`, `fixedStep`) advances by whole fixed steps and only while the world plays : a replay of the run reproduces it exactly, so anything that changes what the game looks like must use it. The wall clock (`realTime`) is the machine's : for what is not part of the simulation (a loading spinner, a cursor blink, a network time-out) and never for what the game decides. The `time_scale` of the engine (slow motion, pause) acts on the first and not on the second.

thread : any, except the setters (main).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_TIME` | `"shard.time"` |  |

#### ShardTimeInfo

```c
uint32_t structSize;
int32_t playing;    // SHARD_TRUE in play mode (always in a player) ; in the editor's edit mode the simulation does not step
uint64_t frame;    // frames run so far
uint64_t fixedStep;    // fixed steps the simulation ran so far : the tick number of a network protocol
double simTime;    // seconds of simulation : fixedStep * fixedDeltaTime, deterministic
double realTime;    // seconds since the engine started, on the wall clock : NOT deterministic
float deltaTime;    // the last frame's variable step, in seconds, before the time scale
float fixedDeltaTime;    // the fixed step, in seconds
float timeScale;    // 1 : real time, 0 : paused, 0.5 : slow motion
float fixedAlpha;    // how far the frame sits between the last fixed step and the next one, in [0, 1) : what to interpolate with
```

#### ShardStateHash

A fingerprint of the simulation after a frame : what two peers compare to know they stayed in step, and what a replay checks. One hash per kind of state, so that the first difference says where to look. Every hash is the same on every platform when the run was.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t reserved;
uint64_t frame;
uint64_t physicsSteps;
uint64_t transforms;    // position, rotation, scale of every actor of the loaded worlds
uint64_t physics;    // pose, velocities and activity of every physics body
uint64_t scripts;    // the declared fields of every script
uint64_t total;    // all of the above
```

#### ShardTimeApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

The caller sets out-&gt;structSize ; the host fills what fits.

```c
ShardResult get(ShardTimeInfo* out);
```

thread : main. 0 pauses the simulation (the frame still runs : UIs, animations in real time...), negative or not finite is `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG`. The scale is the user's to change too (a pause menu) : read it back with get before relying on it.

```c
ShardResult set_time_scale(float scale);
```

thread : main. The fixed step, in seconds (`1/60` by default) : a network game picks the tick rate it has agreed on. Takes effect on the next frame. Changing it while peers run is the game's problem : every peer must change it on the same fixed step.

```c
ShardResult set_fixed_delta_time(float seconds);
```

Hashes the simulation now (between frames : from `on_frame_begin` / `on_frame_end`, a system of the Input or Extract phase, or a job waited for from there). Reads only. thread : main. `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : this host has no engine (an offline tool).

```c
ShardResult state_hash(ShardStateHash* out);
```

### shard_wasm.h

Sandboxed plugins (tier 2, `"abi"`: `"wasm1"`) : the C ABI, for a module built for wasm32 (`docs/design-notes/wasm-sandbox.fr.md`). Experimental : it is not covered by the ABI's compatibility promise yet.

A sandboxed plugin is the plugin you would write for the C ABI (`shard.h`, or `shard/game.hpp` in C++), compiled to WebAssembly. It can touch nothing but its own memory and what the host gives it : no files, no network, no clock, no randomness of the system. It loads without a signature or a consent, because it cannot do more than the host lets it : the interfaces below, filtered by the `"permissions"` of its manifest. Its time (budgets.frameMs per frame) and its memory (budgets.memoryMB) are bounded ; a trap (a division by zero, an access out of its memory, an `unreachable`), an exhausted budget or an import used wrongly stops the plugin, never the engine.

The same source compiles for the engine and for wasm32. This header is all it takes : including it (`shard.h` does, when compiling for wasm) declares every function of the interfaces as an import of the host and builds the tables (`ShardCVarsApi`...) from them. The `ShardHostApi` that `shard_plugin_entry` receives is `shard_wasm_host_table`, which the module exports ; `query_interface` answers from the module's tables. See `shard_wasm_imports.h` (generated from the other headers) for the list.

What differs from a native plugin :

* the interfaces : `shard.plugin`, commands, cvars, components, ecs, systems, events, state, scripts, actors, input, physics, audio, worlds,
```
and shard.content for the plugin's own folder ("fs.read:content"). Not offered : shard.editor, hooks, services, extensions, experimental.
```

* permissions : `shard.content` needs `"fs.read:content"`, `shard.input` `"input"`, `shard.physics` `"physics"`, `shard.audio` `"audio"` (without it
```
query_interface says SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND and the functions answer SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED, or SHARD_FALSE / 0), worlds.load_world
"worlds.load", actors.create / actors.spawn / worlds.spawn_prefab "actors.spawn".
```

* memory of the host is copied : the block of a component that `shard.ecs` hands out, the bytes of a blob and the object of a script
```
live in the module, and what the module changed is copied back when the call that made the copy returns (a system, a script's
callback, a command...). A blob's pointer stays valid until the module resizes or frees the blob. A string the host hands out
(shard.components string_get) is valid until the call returns.
```

* the systems of a module run on the main thread, one after the other : a module is never entered by two threads at once.
* `ShardPluginCtx` : whatever a module passes, an import acts for the plugin the module belongs to.
* `shard.content.read` gives memory that is freed with `ShardHostApi::free` ; resolve and `resolve_logical` (which would give a path of the
```
host) are always SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED, and read / list only reach the plugin's own mod:// address.
```

* the host's alloc and free are the module's memory (they count against budgets.memoryMB).

Building one, in C without a libc :

```
clang --target=wasm32 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -O2 -I<sdk>/include -c plugin.c -o plugin.o
wasm-ld --no-entry --export=shard_plugin_entry --export=shard_wasm_host_table --export-table -o plugin.wasm plugin.o
```

... and in C++ with wasi-sdk (a libc and a libc++ for wasm32, no exceptions) :

```
clang++ --target=wasm32-wasi -fno-exceptions -DSHARD_SDK_NO_EXCEPTIONS -O2 -I<sdk>/include -c a.cpp b.cpp
wasm-ld ... or clang++ -mexec-model=reactor -Wl,--export=shard_plugin_entry -Wl,--export=shard_wasm_host_table -Wl,--export-table
```

`shard_sdk_add_plugin`(... TARGET wasm) does that (`sdk/cmake/ShardSDKPlugin.cmake`). The module must export its memory (`"memory"`, wasm-ld's default) and its function table (`"__indirect_function_table"`, --export-table) : the host reads the arguments of the imports in the first and calls the callbacks through the second. A module with C++ constructors (or a libc to start) exports `_initialize` (wasi-sdk reactors do) or `__wasm_call_ctors` : the host runs it before the entry point. The module's allocator must get its memory from memory.grow, as wasi-libc's does : the host adds pages of its own after the module's.

### shard_worlds.h

Interface `"shard.worlds"` 1.1 : loading worlds, and prefabs ; and which worlds are loaded (1.1).

A world is loaded by its path in the project (`"worlds/arena.world"`). The load is a request : it starts in the background, and the world is swapped in at the start of a following frame, where the old worlds are unloaded (their scripts get `on_destroyed`) and the new one is loaded (the plugin's `on_world_loaded` is called). A script that asks for a load keeps running until then, so nothing it holds is pulled from under it in the middle of a frame.

A prefab is an actor stored as JSON in the content of a module (`prefabs/<name>.json`, `shard_content.h`) : the form the editor writes an actor in. Spawning one builds the actor, its components and its children.

thread : script (`shard_actors.h` says where that is).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_WORLDS` | `"shard.worlds"` |  |

#### ShardWorldsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Asks for that world to replace the loaded ones. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : the project has no such world. `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : a load is already under way (ask again once `is_loading` says it is over). `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : this host has no worlds.

```c
ShardResult load_world(ShardStr path_in_project);
```

`SHARD_TRUE` while a requested load is under way.

```c
int32_t is_loading(void);
```

How many worlds are loaded.

```c
int32_t loaded_count(void);
```

Builds the prefab in the world of `anchor`, under `parent` (0 : at the root), and returns its actor. `prefab` is a `mod://` address (`"mod://com.acme.game/prefabs/crate.json"`), a logical path (`"prefabs/crate.json"`), or a bare name (`"crate"`, read as `"prefabs/crate.json"`). `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : no such file. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : it is not an actor.

```c
ShardResult spawn_prefab(ShardActor anchor, ShardStr prefab, ShardActor parent, ShardActor* out);
```

**1.1**

The loaded world at an index (0 .. `loaded_count` - 1, the order they were loaded in) : its asset id (-1 if it has none), its name as a `"text out"`, and an actor to use as the `anchor` of the functions that work `"in the world of"` one -- its first root actor, or 0 if the world is empty. Any of the pointers may be NULL. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : past the end.

```c
ShardResult world_at(int32_t index, int32_t* asset_id, char* name, uint64_t capacity, uint64_t* size, ShardActor* anchor);
```

## The C++ SDK

`sdk/include/shard/cpp` : header-only C++17 over the C ABI, compiled into the plugin. `#include <shard/cpp/plugin.hpp>` brings all of it. Every callback of the SDK catches what the plugin throws : `Shard::Error` (what a registration the host refused throws, with its `ShardResult`) and anything else become an error of that callback, with the message in the log. Below, the public declarations of each header (bodies left out).

### shard/cpp/plugin.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : a plugin class over the C ABI.

```cpp
class SpinPlugin : public Shard::Plugin {
public:
    void OnLoad(Shard::Context& ctx) override { ... }
};
SHARD_C_PLUGIN(SpinPlugin)
```

The macro exports `shard_plugin_entry` and fills the callbacks table : every callback catches what the plugin throws (`Shard::Error` from a refused registration, or anything else) and turns it into an error the host fails the plugin with, the message in its log. Nothing of the engine is included or linked : this compiles against `sdk/include` alone, with any C++17 compiler.

#### `Context`

What the host knows of the plugin, and every way the plugin reaches it

```cpp
ShardPluginCtx Handle() const;
std::string_view Id() const;
std::string_view Version() const;
/// The plugin's folder, absolute
std::string_view Directory() const;
/// "editor", "player", "headless" or "tool" (empty in an engine of ABI 1.0)
std::string_view HostName() const;
/// True if the manifest asks for that permission (false in an engine of ABI 1.0)
bool HasPermission(std::string_view permission) const;
void Log(std::string_view message) const;
void Warn(std::string_view message) const;
void Error(std::string_view message) const;
/// Memory counted against the plugin's budget (manifest budgets.memoryMB) : give it back with Free
void* Alloc(size_t size, size_t align = 16) const;
void Free(void* p) const;
Shard::Components Components() const;
Shard::Systems Systems() const;
Shard::Scripts Scripts() const;
Shard::Editor Editor() const;
Shard::CVars CVars() const;
Shard::Commands Commands() const;
Shard::Events Events() const;
Shard::Hooks Hooks() const;
Shard::Services Services() const;
Shard::Content Content() const;
Shard::Extensions Extensions() const;
Shard::Reflect Reflect() const;
```

#### `World`

A world a module is told about

```cpp
int32_t assetId = -1;
std::string_view name;
```

#### `Plugin`

The base of a plugin written with the SDK : the same calls, in the same order, as the engine's IPlugin (see `shard_host.h`)

```cpp
/// Register everything here (components, systems, cvars, commands, services, hooks...)
virtual void OnLoad(Context&);
/// Every plugin ran OnLoad : the services of the others can be asked for
virtual void OnInitialize(Context&);
virtual void OnEnable(Context&);
virtual void OnDisable(Context&);
virtual void OnUnload(Context&);
/// Hot reload : write what must survive and return true ; false (the default) makes the plugin not reloadable
virtual bool OnPrepareReload(Context&, StateWriter&);
virtual void OnRestore(Context&, StateReader&);
virtual void OnFrameBegin(Context&, uint64_t /*frame*/);
virtual void OnFrameEnd(Context&, uint64_t /*frame*/);
virtual void OnContentMounted(Context&);
virtual void OnWorldLoaded(Context&, const World&);
virtual void OnWorldUnloaded(Context&, const World&);
virtual void OnPlayStart(Context&, const World&);
virtual void OnPlayStop(Context&, const World&);
/// An offline tool is about to run `task` ("cook", "bake", "validate") : return false (and a message) to cancel it
virtual bool OnToolTask(Context&, std::string_view /*task*/, std::string_view /*project*/, std::string& /*message*/);
```

```cpp
/// Exports the entry point of the C ABI for a class derived from Shard::Plugin (once per plugin, in one source file)
SHARD_C_PLUGIN(ClassName)
/// A plugin that is only what its source files register (scripts, components, systems: shard/cpp/registry.hpp): the entry point, in any one of them
SHARD_GAME_MODULE()
```

### shard/cpp/component.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : component types from C++ structs.

```cpp
struct Spin { float speed = 1.f; float angle = 0.f; Shard::Vec3 axis{ 0.f, 1.f, 0.f }; };
SHARD_COMPONENT(Spin, (speed)(angle)(axis))
```

(at global scope) declares which members are fields (their type and offset are deduced) ; the struct's default member values are the defaults of a new component. The struct must be trivially copyable and standard layout : it is the block the engine copies with memcpy (`shard_components.h`). Register it in OnLoad with `ctx.Components().Register<Spin>("Spin")`.

#### `Vec2`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f;
```

#### `Vec3`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f, z = 0.f;
```

#### `Vec4`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f, z = 0.f, w = 0.f;
```

#### `Quat`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f, z = 0.f, w = 1.f;
```

#### `Color`

```cpp
float r = 1.f, g = 1.f, b = 1.f, a = 1.f;
```

#### `FieldType<float>, FieldType<double>, FieldType<int32_t>, FieldType<uint32_t>, FieldType<int64_t>, FieldType<uint64_t>, FieldType<bool>, FieldType<Vec2>, FieldType<Vec3>, FieldType<Vec4>, FieldType<Quat>, FieldType<Color>, FieldType<float[2]>, FieldType<float[3]>, FieldType<float[4]>, FieldType<Blob>, FieldType<std::string>, FieldType<Text>, FieldType<AssetId>`

The `SHARD_FIELD_*` of a member type. Specialize it for a type of your own with the same layout (`glm::vec3` -&gt; `SHARD_FIELD_VEC3`).

```cpp
static constexpr uint32_t value = 0;
```

#### `Blob`

A blob of this plugin (`shard_components.h`, 1.1) : bytes the host keeps outside a component's block, as many as needed. A component holds one in a member of this type ; `Components::CreateBlob` makes it. Copying the struct copies the handle, not the bytes.

```cpp
ShardBlob handle = 0;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

#### `FieldFlags`

Flags a member type adds to its field : none, except for a `std::string` of a script, which the host reads through the script's callbacks

```cpp
static constexpr uint32_t value = 0;
```

#### `Text`

A text of a component (`shard_components.h`, 1.2) : a field of this type holds a handle, the text lives in the host. The inspector shows it as a text box and the world file saves it as a string. Read it with `Components::GetText`, write it with `Components::SetText`. Copying the struct copies the handle, not the text.

```cpp
ShardBlob handle = 0;
/// The text (empty if there is none yet). thread : any
std::string Get() const;
/// Replaces the text. Throws Shard::Error over the memory budget, or in an engine older than ABI 1.3. thread : any
void Set(std::string_view text);
Text& operator=(std::string_view text);
Text& operator=(const char* text);
Text& operator=(const std::string& text);
Text& operator=(const Text&) = default;
```

#### `AssetId`

The id of an asset of the project (`shard_components.h`, 1.2), 0 for none : the inspector shows an asset picker

```cpp
int32_t id = 0;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

#### `FieldOptions`

How a field shows in the editor and whether it is saved (see `shard_components.h`)

```cpp
/// the member's name, as written in SHARD_COMPONENT
std::string name;
/// SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME, SHARD_FIELD_PRIVATE
uint32_t flags = 0;
float min = 0.f, max = 0.f;
std::string tooltip;
/// Only the name is required : { "speed", 0, 0.f, 100.f }, { "frames", SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME }
FieldOptions(std::string fieldName, uint32_t fieldFlags = 0, float lowest = 0.f, float highest = 0.f, std::string hint = {}) : name(std::move(fieldName)), flags(fieldFlags), min(lowest), max(highest), tooltip(std::move(hint));
```

#### `ComponentEvents`

What a plugin is told about the actor components of a type (ABI 1.4 of `shard.components`) : `block` is the component's values, on the main thread, in the editor's edit mode as well as in play mode.

```
onAdded    : the component is on a live entity of an active actor. What you change in `block` is pushed to the entity afterwards.
```

onRemoved  : it is about to leave (removed, its actor destroyed or deactivated, the world unloaded) ; the block is still intact. onChanged  : a field was edited (inspector, SetComponentJson) ; `field` is its index among the registered fields. `actor` is the Actor that carries it, `entity` its ECS entity (`shard.ecs`).

```cpp
std::function<void(uint64_t actor, uint64_t entity, T& block)> onAdded;
std::function<void(uint64_t actor, uint64_t entity, T& block)> onRemoved;
std::function<void(uint64_t actor, uint64_t entity, T& block, uint32_t field)> onChanged;
```

### shard/cpp/system.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : systems and what they see of the entities.

```cpp
ctx.Systems().Add("rotate", Shard::Phase::Update)
    .Writes(spin)
    .Run([spin](Shard::SystemCtx& s) {
        s.Each(spin, [&](Spin& c) { c.angle += c.speed * s.DeltaTime(); });
    });
```

A system reads and writes only the types it declared (Reads / Writes) : the scheduler runs systems in parallel on that promise.

```cpp
using Entity = ShardEntity;
enum class Phase : uint32_t { Input = SHARD_PHASE_INPUT, PreSim = SHARD_PHASE_PRE_SIM, Fixed = SHARD_PHASE_FIXED, PostPhysics = SHARD_PHASE_POST_PHYSICS, Update = SHARD_PHASE_UPDATE, Late = SHARD_PHASE_LATE, Extract = SHARD_PHASE_EXTRACT, };
```

### shard/cpp/services.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : services between plugins (`shard_services.h`). A service is a C table of function pointers that starts with `uint32_t structSize`, published in a header by its provider :

```cpp
struct WeatherApi { uint32_t structSize; float (SHARD_CALL *rain)(void* self, float x, float z); };
ctx.Services().Provide("weather.query", 1, 0, &kWeatherApi, this);                 // the provider
auto weather = ctx.Services().Get<WeatherApi>("weather.query", "^1");              // a user, in OnInitialize
if (auto w = weather.Resolve()) w.table->rain(w.self, 0.f, 0.f);                   // before each use
```

#### `Resolved`

A service resolved now : its table and the provider's `self`. Do not keep it : resolve again before each use.

```cpp
const Table* table = nullptr;
void* self = nullptr;
uint32_t major = 0, minor = 0;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

#### `Service`

A handle on a service : empty once its provider is disabled or unloaded


### shard/cpp/actor.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : actors, the things a world holds (`shard_actors.h`).

```cpp
Shard::Actor enemy = scene.Spawn(R"({ "name": "Enemy", "components": [] })");
enemy.SetPosition({ 0.f, 1.f, -5.f });
enemy.AddTag("Enemy");
if (Health* health = enemy.GetScript<Health>()) health->Damage(10.f);
```

An Actor is a handle: copying it is free, and it stays safe when the actor is destroyed (`IsValid()` turns false, the getters return zeroes, the setters do nothing). Use it from the callbacks of a script (`Shard::Script`) : not from a system, which runs beside others.

The world an actor is in: where to create, spawn and find other actors

### shard/cpp/assets.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : the assets of the project, by path and by id (`shard_assets.h`).

```cpp
if (auto id = Shard::Assets::Resolve("models/level.fbx")) {
    if (auto mesh = Shard::Assets::ReadMesh(*id)) Bake(mesh->positions, mesh->indices);       // a navigation mesh from the level's triangles
}
Shard::Assets::Write("navigation/level.nav", bytes.data(), bytes.size());                      // a file of the project, indexed as an asset
```

A path is a path in the project (`"models/crate.fbx"`) ; a `mod://` address is accepted wherever a file is read. thread : main unless said otherwise.

### shard/cpp/audio.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : sounds (`shard_audio.h`). An actor with an `"audio"` component plays and pauses its clip with `Actor::PlayAudio`, PauseAudio and SetAudioVolume. A one shot sound needs no actor.

```cpp
Shard::Audio::PlayOneShot("sounds/shot.wav", Owner().WorldPosition());
```

```cpp
/// Plays a clip of the project ("sounds/shot.wav") once, from `position` in the world when `spatial` (louder and panned by the distance
/// and direction to the listener), flat otherwise. The sound removes itself when it ends. Throws Shard::Error if there is no such clip.
static void PlayOneShot(std::string_view clip, Vec3 position, float volume = 1.f, bool spatial = true);
/// A flat sound, with no place
```

### shard/cpp/debug.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : drawing for the developer, in the world, from anywhere (`shard_debug.h`).

```cpp
Shard::Debug::Line(agent.position, agent.destination, Shard::Rgba(0, 255, 0));                 // for this frame
Shard::Debug::Sphere(sensor.center, sensor.radius, Shard::Rgba(255, 255, 0, 128), 2.f);        // for two seconds
if (Shard::Debug::Enabled()) for (const auto& edge : navmesh.Edges()) Shard::Debug::Line(edge.a, edge.b, kEdge);
```

A shape lives `duration` seconds (0 : one frame), so a system that draws what it computes calls the functions again every frame. thread : any.

```cpp
/// 8 bit r, g, b, a packed as the ABI wants
constexpr uint32_t Rgba(uint32_t r, uint32_t g, uint32_t b, uint32_t a = 255);
```

### shard/cpp/editor.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : windows of the editor (`shard_editor.h`).

```cpp
SHARD_EDITOR_PANEL(Spawner, "Enemy spawner", ui)
{
    static int count = 5;
    ui.SliderInt("Count", count, 1, 50);
    if (ui.Button("Spawn")) SpawnEnemies(count);
}
```

The panel appears in the editor's Window menu. Menu items (`SHARD_EDITOR_MENU_ITEM`), toolbar buttons, inspectors below a component, gizmos in the viewport and the selection are in the same header. In the player, in headless runs and in the offline tools there is no editor : the panel is not added and nothing else changes, so the same plugin runs everywhere. A plugin whose manifest hosts include `"engine"` is loaded by the editor ; `"editor"` alone limits it to the editor.

### shard/cpp/engine_components.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : the engine's own components (model, light, physics body...) as typed handles, over `shard.actors`' field functions.

```cpp
Shard::Actor bullet = GetScene().Create("Bullet");

auto model = bullet.Add<Shard::Model>();
model.SetMesh(mesh);                                       // an AssetId (a field of the script), or the asset's name in the project
model.SetMaterial(0, material);

auto body = bullet.Add<Shard::PhysicsBody>();
body.SetShape(Shard::Shape::Capsule(0.1f, 0.3f));
body.SetMotionType(Shard::MotionType::Dynamic);            // the body of the new kind exists at once : the velocity has something to push
body.SetFriction(0.8f);
bullet.SetVelocity(forward * 30.f);

if (auto light = bullet.Get<Shard::Light>()) light.SetIntensity(3.f);
```

A handle is a pair (actor, component type) : copying it is free, and it stays safe when the actor goes. Every setter changes that one field and nothing else, the way an edit in the inspector does (the component's own change hook runs : a body keeps its velocity when its friction changes) and throws `Shard::Error` when the engine refuses it. The getters return a zero when the component or the field is gone.

Not every component has a class here : `Shard::ComponentRef` reaches any field of any component of the engine by its name (the one the inspector and the world file use) :

```cpp
Shard::ComponentRef probe(actor, "probeVolume");
probe.SetFloat("blendDistance", 2.f);
```

Assets read as their name in the project (the way a world file stores them) and are set from an AssetId or from that name.

```cpp
/// An enum of the engine's components, as the names the inspector shows
enum class MotionType { Static, Kinematic, Dynamic };
enum class GravityMode { Fields, World, Custom };
enum class LightType { Directional, Point, Spot };
enum class BakeMode { Dynamic, Stationary, Static };
enum class BillboardFacing { Camera, AxisY, Fixed };
```

#### `ComponentRef`

One component of an actor, reached by the names of its fields. The classes below (Model, PhysicsBody...) are this with the names written for you ; use it directly for a component that has no class here.

```cpp
/// `type` is the name the world file gives the component ("light", "physics_body", or "<plugin id>.<script>"). It must outlive the handle
/// (a literal).
ComponentRef(Actor actor, const char* type) : m_Actor(actor), m_Type(type);
const Actor& Owner() const;
const char* Type() const;
/// The actor is alive and still has the component
bool IsValid() const;
explicit operator bool() const;
/// Removes the component from its actor
bool Remove() const;
/// A deactivated component does nothing, as if it were not there
bool IsActive() const;
void SetActive(bool active) const;
/// The value as JSON text ; empty if the component or the field is not there
std::string GetJson(std::string_view path) const;
/// Sets the field to a value written as JSON text. Throws Shard::Error.
void SetJson(std::string_view path, std::string_view valueJson) const;
/// Removes an element of an array field (path "shapes/1") or a key of an object. Throws Shard::Error.
void Erase(std::string_view path) const;
void SetFloat(std::string_view path, float value) const;
void SetInt(std::string_view path, int64_t value) const;
void SetBool(std::string_view path, bool value) const;
void SetString(std::string_view path, std::string_view value) const;
void SetVec3(std::string_view path, Vec3 v) const;
void SetColor(std::string_view path, Color c) const;
/// An asset, by its id (0 : none) or by its name in the project
void SetAsset(std::string_view path, AssetId asset) const;
void SetAsset(std::string_view path, std::string_view assetName) const;
/// An enum, by the name the inspector shows ("Dynamic")
void SetEnum(std::string_view path, std::string_view name) const;
float GetFloat(std::string_view path, float fallback = 0.f) const;
int64_t GetInt(std::string_view path, int64_t fallback = 0) const;
bool GetBool(std::string_view path, bool fallback = false) const;
std::string GetString(std::string_view path) const;
Vec3 GetVec3(std::string_view path) const;
Color GetColor(std::string_view path) const;
/// The name in the project of an asset field ; empty for none
std::string GetAsset(std::string_view path) const;
/// The name of the value of an enum field ("Dynamic")
std::string GetEnum(std::string_view path) const;
/// How many elements an array field holds
size_t Count(std::string_view path) const;
```

#### `Shape`

A shape of a physics body. Dimensions are in the body's own space, before the actor's scale.

```cpp
enum class Kind { Sphere, Box, Capsule, Cylinder };
Kind kind = Kind::Box;
/// sphere, capsule, cylinder
float radius = 0.5f;
/// capsule (without its caps), cylinder : it lies along the body's Y
float halfHeight = 0.5f;
Vec3 halfExtent{ 0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f };
/// where the shape sits in the body
Vec3 offset;
/// how it is turned in the body
Quat rotation;
static Shape Sphere(float radius = 0.5f);
static Shape Box(Vec3 halfExtent = { 0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f });
static Shape Capsule(float radius = 0.5f, float halfHeight = 0.5f);
static Shape Cylinder(float radius = 0.5f, float halfHeight = 0.5f);
/// The same shape, moved and turned inside the body
Shape At(Vec3 where, Quat turned = Quat()) const;
std::string ToJson() const;
```

#### `PhysicsBody`

`"physics_body"` : the actor is simulated (or collides, if it is static). Velocities and forces are on the Actor.

```cpp
static constexpr const char* kType = "physics_body";
PhysicsBody() = default;
explicit PhysicsBody(Actor actor) : ComponentRef(actor, kType);
/// Static never moves, Kinematic is moved by code only, Dynamic is driven by the simulation. The body is rebuilt as the new kind at once.
void SetMotionType(MotionType type) const;
MotionType GetMotionType() const;
/// Replaces the shapes of the body by this one (the body is rebuilt, which drops its velocity)
void SetShape(const Shape& shape) const;
/// Adds a shape to the body (a compound : the body is rebuilt)
void AddShape(const Shape& shape) const;
/// Removes a shape ; a body keeps at least one
void RemoveShape(size_t index) const;
size_t ShapeCount() const;
/// The mass in kg. Without it the mass comes from the shape (and the engine's density).
void SetMass(float kilograms) const;
float Mass() const;
void UseShapeMass() const;
void SetLinearDamping(float damping) const;
float LinearDamping() const;
void SetAngularDamping(float damping) const;
float AngularDamping() const;
/// A multiplier on the gravity the body feels : 0 floats, a negative one falls upwards
void SetGravityFactor(float factor) const;
float GravityFactor() const;
/// Fields : the world's gravity changed by the gravity fields around. World ignores the fields. Custom is SetCustomGravity's.
void SetGravityMode(GravityMode mode) const;
void SetCustomGravity(Vec3 acceleration) const;
/// Resistance when sliding : 0 is ice, 1 is very grippy
void SetFriction(float friction) const;
float Friction() const;
/// Bounciness : 0 does not bounce, 1 gives back all its energy
void SetRestitution(float restitution) const;
float Restitution() const;
```

### shard/cpp/field.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : the fields of a script, declared where the member is.

```cpp
class Gun : public Shard::Script {
public:
    SHARD_FIELD(float, power, Range(0.f, 1000.f), Tooltip("Speed of the bullet")) = 30.f;
    SHARD_FIELD(float, lifetime, Range(0.f, 60.f)) = 3.f;
    SHARD_FIELD(Shard::AssetId, mesh, Tooltip("The mesh to shoot"));
    SHARD_FIELD(int, ammo, Runtime()) = 12;                  // shown by the inspector, not saved
    float cooldown = 0.f;                                    // not a field : it stays out of the inspector and the world file
};

// gun.cpp
SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Gun)
```

The macro declares the member (`Type name`, so the default value goes after it, as for any member) and, in front of it, a one byte member that tells the SDK its name, its type, where it is in the object and its options. Nothing else lists the field : no sequence in the .cpp, no generated file. Options are the names below, written bare inside the macro:

```cpp
Range(min, max)     the bounds of the inspector's widget
Tooltip("text")     what the inspector shows when the mouse rests on the field
Runtime()           the inspector shows it, read only, and the world file does not save it
Hidden()            neither shown nor saved (the object keeps it; not for a string)
```

The type is any of the field types of `shard/cpp/component.hpp` (numbers, bool, `Vec2/3/4`, Quat, Color, Text, AssetId, `std::string`, Actor, Blob).

#### `FieldSpec`

What the options of a field add to it

```cpp
uint32_t flags = 0;
float min = 0.f, max = 0.f;
std::string tooltip;
```

#### `Range`

```cpp
float min, max;
void Apply(FieldSpec& spec) const;
```

#### `Tooltip`

```cpp
const char* text;
void Apply(FieldSpec& spec) const;
```

#### `Runtime`

```cpp
void Apply(FieldSpec& spec) const;
```

#### `Hidden`

```cpp
void Apply(FieldSpec& spec) const;
```

#### `End`

`SHARD_FIELD` ends its options with it, so that the macro never has an empty `"..."` (an error in C++17 with -pedantic)

```cpp
void Apply(FieldSpec&) const;
```

```cpp
template <typename... Options> FieldSpec MakeFieldSpec(const Options&... options);
/// Declares a field of a script : `SHARD_FIELD(float, power, Range(0.f, 1000.f)) = 30.f;` (options are optional, see the top of this file)
SHARD_FIELD(...)
```

Shard C++ SDK : keyboard, mouse and gamepads (`shard_input.h`).

```cpp

const float turn = Shard::Input::Axis(Shard::Key::A, Shard::Key::D);                 // -1, 0 or 1
if (Shard::Input::WasPressed(Shard::Key::Space)) Jump();
```

What the engine's input manager sees this frame, which is also what a replay records. Call it from the callbacks of a script.

### shard/cpp/jobs.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : the engine's worker threads (`shard_jobs.h`).

```cpp
// bake something off the frame, then hand the result to the simulation
auto job = Shard::Jobs::Run([chunk](uint32_t /*worker*/) { chunk->BuildMesh(); });
...
job.Wait();                                           // or let it go: ~JobHandle releases it, the work still runs to its end

Shard::Jobs::ParallelFor(agents.size(), [&](uint32_t i, uint32_t /*worker*/) { agents[i].Steer(dt); });     // returns when all are done
Shard::Jobs::PostMain([] { /* back on the main thread, at the start of the next frame */ });
```

A job may call what the headers document as `"thread : any"` (blobs, `shard.render`'s resources, `shard.debug`, the maths...) and the plugin's own code, not the actors, the ECS, the physics or the input (they are made for the thread of the simulation). A job that is still running when the plugin is disabled is waited for first.

#### `JobHandle`

A job (or the slices of a ParallelForAsync) in flight. Move only ; letting go of it does not stop the work.

```cpp
JobHandle& operator=(JobHandle&& other) noexcept;
JobHandle& operator=(const JobHandle&) = delete;
/// True once the work ended (a default handle, or one that ran inline, is done)
bool IsDone() const;
/// Returns when the work ended, running other jobs meanwhile. thread : main, script or system
void Wait();
```

#### `Jobs`

```cpp
/// The threads that work for the engine, the calling one included : the size of a per-worker scratch array
static uint32_t WorkerCount();
/// Runs `fn(worker)` on a worker. Keep the handle to Wait for it ; drop it to let the job go on its own.
template <typename F> static JobHandle Run(F&& fn);
/// The same, without a handle : nothing will wait for it
template <typename F> static void RunDetached(F&& fn);
/// Calls `fn(index, worker)` for every index of [0, count), on every worker at once, and returns when all are done. The order is not defined :
/// write to a slot per index, combine in index order. `grain` : how many indices a slice has (0 : the host picks).
template <typename F> static void ParallelFor(uint32_t count, F&& fn, uint32_t grain = 0);
/// `fn(begin, end, worker)` on slices of [0, count) : for a body with a setup per slice
template <typename F> static void ParallelForRange(uint32_t count, F&& fn, uint32_t grain = 0);
/// The same, without waiting : the closure is kept until the last slice ended
template <typename F> static JobHandle ParallelForAsync(uint32_t count, F&& fn, uint32_t grain = 0);
/// Runs `fn()` on the main thread at the start of the next frame : how a job hands its result to the simulation. thread : any
template <typename F> static void PostMain(F&& fn);
```

### shard/cpp/math.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : the small math a gameplay script needs, on the plain structs of the ABI (Vec2, Vec3, Vec4, Quat, Color, Pose).

The types are aggregates (Vec3{ 1, 2, 3 }), laid out like the engine's own, so a field of a script or a component can be one. The functions are free functions in namespace shard; the usual operators work. Conventions are the engine's: right handed, Y up, an actor looks down -Z, angles in radians (the Degrees helpers convert), quaternions x, y, z, w.

```cpp
constexpr float kPi = 3.14159265358979323846f;
constexpr float Radians(float degrees);
constexpr float Degrees(float radians);
template <typename T> constexpr T Clamp(T v, T lo, T hi);
constexpr float Lerp(float a, float b, float t);
constexpr Vec2 operator+(Vec2 a, Vec2 b);
constexpr Vec2 operator-(Vec2 a, Vec2 b);
constexpr Vec2 operator*(Vec2 a, float k);
constexpr Vec2 operator*(float k, Vec2 a);
constexpr Vec2 operator/(Vec2 a, float k);
constexpr Vec2 operator-(Vec2 a);
constexpr float Dot(Vec2 a, Vec2 b);
inline float Length(Vec2 a);
constexpr Vec3 operator+(Vec3 a, Vec3 b);
constexpr Vec3 operator-(Vec3 a, Vec3 b);
constexpr Vec3 operator*(Vec3 a, float k);
constexpr Vec3 operator*(float k, Vec3 a);
constexpr Vec3 operator*(Vec3 a, Vec3 b);
constexpr Vec3 operator/(Vec3 a, float k);
constexpr Vec3 operator-(Vec3 a);
inline Vec3& operator+=(Vec3& a, Vec3 b);
inline Vec3& operator-=(Vec3& a, Vec3 b);
inline Vec3& operator*=(Vec3& a, float k);
constexpr bool operator==(Vec3 a, Vec3 b);
constexpr bool operator!=(Vec3 a, Vec3 b);
constexpr float Dot(Vec3 a, Vec3 b);
constexpr Vec3 Cross(Vec3 a, Vec3 b);
constexpr float LengthSquared(Vec3 a);
inline float Length(Vec3 a);
inline float Distance(Vec3 a, Vec3 b);
/// The unit vector with that direction (the zero vector stays zero)
inline Vec3 Normalize(Vec3 a);
constexpr Vec3 Lerp(Vec3 a, Vec3 b, float t);
/// `v` moved toward `target` by at most `maxDelta`
inline Vec3 MoveTowards(Vec3 v, Vec3 target, float maxDelta);
constexpr Quat operator*(Quat a, Quat b);
constexpr Quat Conjugate(Quat q);
inline Quat Normalize(Quat q);
/// The vector rotated by the quaternion
constexpr Vec3 operator*(Quat q, Vec3 v);
inline Quat AxisAngle(Vec3 axis, float radians);
/// Rotations about X (pitch), Y (yaw) then Z (roll), in degrees: applied in the order yaw, pitch, roll as a first person camera expects
inline Quat FromEulerDegrees(float pitch, float yaw, float roll);
/// The rotation that turns an actor's forward (-Z) toward `direction`, keeping `up` up
inline Quat LookRotation(Vec3 direction, Vec3 up = { 0.f, 1.f, 0.f });
inline Quat Slerp(Quat a, Quat b, float t);
```

An actor's pose: the layout of `ShardLocalTransform` (position, rotation, scale)

### shard/cpp/net.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : UDP and TCP sockets, for the networking a game builds itself (`shard_net.h`).

```cpp
// a server : datagrams on a port
Shard::Net::UdpSocket server = Shard::Net::OpenUdp(27015, [&](const Shard::Net::Event& e) {
    if (e.kind == Shard::Net::EventKind::Data) HandleDatagram(e.peer, e.data, e.size);
});
server.SendTo({ "192.0.2.7", 27016 }, bytes.data(), bytes.size());

// a client : a stream
Shard::Net::TcpSocket client = Shard::Net::Connect({ "example.com", 4000 }, [&](const Shard::Net::Event& e) { ... });
```

The events arrive on the main thread, at the start of the frame (`Net::Poll`() reads just before a fixed step). The plugin declares the permission `"net"` in its manifest. The sockets close with the object, and with the plugin.

```cpp
enum class EventKind : uint32_t { Connected = SHARD_NET_EVENT_CONNECTED, Accepted = SHARD_NET_EVENT_ACCEPTED, Data = SHARD_NET_EVENT_DATA, Closed = SHARD_NET_EVENT_CLOSED, Error = SHARD_NET_EVENT_ERROR };
```

#### `Address`

```cpp
/// a dotted address, a name, or empty (any local address, to bind)
std::string host;
uint32_t port = 0;
```

#### `Event`

```cpp
EventKind kind = EventKind::Data;
/// Accepted : the new connection
ShardSocket socket = 0;
/// Accepted : the listener
ShardSocket listener = 0;
/// "192.0.2.7:4000" ; valid during the callback
std::string_view peer;
/// Data : valid during the callback
const void* data = nullptr;
uint64_t size = 0;
int32_t error = 0;
```

```cpp
using Handler = std::function<void(const Event&)>;
inline const ShardNetApi& Api();
inline void Thunk(void* user, ShardPluginCtx, const ShardNetEvent* e);
inline ShardNetAddress Convert(const Address& a);
```

#### `Socket`

A socket the plugin owns : closed with the object. A TCP socket accepted by a listener is wrapped with `Socket::Adopt`.

```cpp
Socket& operator=(Socket&& o) noexcept;
Socket& operator=(const Socket&) = delete;
explicit operator bool() const;
ShardSocket Handle() const;
/// TCP : queues the bytes. False if the queue is full (nothing was queued) or the socket is closed.
bool Send(const void* data, uint64_t size) const;
bool Send(std::string_view bytes) const;
/// UDP : one datagram
bool SendTo(const Address& to, const void* data, uint64_t size) const;
uint32_t LocalPort() const;
uint64_t QueuedBytes() const;
bool SetOption(uint32_t option, int32_t value) const;
void Close();
/// A connection a listener accepted (Event::socket of an Accepted event) : it reports to the listener's handler, `handler` is not used for it
static Socket Adopt(ShardSocket socket);
```

```cpp
using UdpSocket = Socket;
using TcpSocket = Socket;
/// A UDP socket bound to `port` (0 : any free port, LocalPort() says which). Throws Shard::Error if the address is in use or the plugin is over its limit.
inline Socket OpenUdp(uint32_t port, Handler handler, std::string_view host = {});
/// Listens for TCP connections ; each client is an Accepted event
inline Socket Listen(const Address& bind, Handler handler, int backlog = 16);
/// Starts connecting (the name is resolved off the frame) : the outcome is a Connected or an Error event. Bytes sent meanwhile are queued.
inline Socket Connect(const Address& remote, Handler handler);
/// Reads the sockets now and delivers what arrived (the host also does it at the start of every frame)
inline void Poll();
```

### shard/cpp/physics.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : ray casts (`shard_physics.h`). The forces, impulses and velocities of a body are methods of `Shard::Actor`.

```cpp
if (auto hit = Shard::Physics::Raycast(eye, forward, 50.f, Shard::Layers::All, Owner())) {
    hit->actor.Destroy();
    Spawn(hit->point + hit->normal * 0.1f);
}
```

#### `Layers`

Which bodies a ray looks at

```cpp
/// bodies that never move
static constexpr uint32_t Static = SHARD_LAYER_STATIC;
/// kinematic and dynamic bodies
static constexpr uint32_t Moving = SHARD_LAYER_MOVING;
static constexpr uint32_t All = SHARD_LAYER_ALL;
```

#### `RayHit`

```cpp
/// the actor whose body was hit (invalid for a collider with no owner)
Actor actor;
/// where, in the world
Vec3 point;
/// the surface normal there, pointing out of the body ; for an overlap, the way to push the shape out
Vec3 normal;
/// from the origin along the ray ; for an overlap, how deep the shapes overlap
float distance = 0.f;
/// a collider of the plugin that was hit (ABI 1.7), 0 for the body of an actor
ShardCollider collider = 0;
/// that collider's userData
uint64_t userData = 0;
/// a mesh collider : the index of the triangle
uint32_t triangle = 0;
/// a box set : the index of the box
uint32_t box = 0;
```

#### `QueryFilter`

What a query looks at (ABI 1.7)

```cpp
uint32_t layers = Layers::All;
/// an actor whose body the query goes through
Actor ignore;
/// only the colliders of plugins
bool collidersOnly = false;
/// only the bodies of actors
bool noColliders = false;
/// only the actors that have this tag (or one under it)
std::string tag;
```

#### `Collider`

A static collider the plugin builds (a voxel chunk, a navigation obstacle, a heightfield cut into a mesh) : it exists in the physics world with no actor and goes with the object. It appears at the next fixed step. (ABI 1.7)

```cpp
Collider& operator=(Collider&& o) noexcept;
Collider& operator=(const Collider&) = delete;
/// Triangles : `vertices` 3 floats each, `indices` a triangle list. thread : any (a mesh shape can take a while : build it in a job).
static Collider Mesh(const float* vertices, uint32_t vertexCount, const uint32_t* indices, uint32_t indexCount, Vec3 position = {}, Quat rotation = {}, uint64_t userData = 0, Actor owner = Actor());
/// A union of boxes aligned on the collider axes : 6 floats each (centre xyz, half extent xyz)
static Collider Boxes(const float* boxes, uint32_t boxCount, Vec3 position = {}, Quat rotation = {}, uint64_t userData = 0, Actor owner = Actor());
explicit operator bool() const;
ShardCollider Handle() const;
bool SetPose(Vec3 position, Quat rotation = {}) const;
/// Replaces the geometry (a chunk was edited) with a new mesh
bool UpdateMesh(const float* vertices, uint32_t vertexCount, const uint32_t* indices, uint32_t indexCount) const;
void Reset();
```

#### `Physics`

```cpp
/// The first body the ray meets within `maxDistance`. `direction` need not be normalized. `ignore` : an actor whose body the ray goes
/// through, usually the one that fires it. Call it from the callbacks of a script.
static std::optional<RayHit> Raycast(Vec3 origin, Vec3 direction, float maxDistance, uint32_t layers = Layers::All, Actor ignore = Actor());
/// Every body along the ray, nearest first
static std::vector<RayHit> RaycastAll(Vec3 origin, Vec3 direction, float maxDistance, const QueryFilter& filter = {});
/// The bodies that touch the shape
static std::vector<RayHit> OverlapSphere(Vec3 center, float radius, const QueryFilter& filter = {});
static std::vector<RayHit> OverlapBox(Vec3 center, Vec3 halfExtent, Quat rotation = {}, const QueryFilter& filter = {});
static std::vector<RayHit> OverlapCapsule(Vec3 from, Vec3 to, float radius, const QueryFilter& filter = {});
/// The first body a sphere meets going along `direction` : `distance` is how far it got
```

### shard/cpp/random.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : random numbers that a replay of the run reproduces (`shard_plugin.h`, `random_stream`).

```cpp
class Kicker : public Shard::Script {
    void OnPlay() override { m_Random = Shard::Random::Stream("Kicker/" + Owner().Name()); }
    void OnTick(float) override { Owner().AddImpulse(m_Random.OnUnitSphere() * 4.f); }
    Shard::Random m_Random;
};
```

`rand()`, `std::random_device` and `std::uniform_`\*\_distribution give different numbers from one run, platform or standard library to the next, so a replay or a networked simulation that used them would drift. A stream starts from the run's seed, and this class (PCG32, the generator of the engine's own `Core::Random`) produces the same numbers everywhere. Not for cryptography.

#### `Random`

```cpp
/// A generator with a fixed seed, for what does not depend on the run (the same sequence in every run)
constexpr Random() : m_State(0x853c49e6748fea9bull), m_Increment(0xda3e39cb94b95bdbull);
/// The stream `name` of this plugin for this run : the same name gives the same sequence when the run is replayed, and another name a
/// sequence that does not depend on it. Name it after what draws from it ("Spawner/" + the actor's name), not after the order things
/// started in. Throws Shard::Error if the host does not offer streams (an engine of ABI 1.4 or older).
static Random Stream(std::string_view name);
/// Uniform 32 random bits
uint32_t Next();
/// Uniform in [0, bound), without modulo bias. bound == 0 returns 0
uint32_t Below(uint32_t bound);
/// Uniform integer in [lo, hi], both included
int32_t Range(int32_t lo, int32_t hi);
/// Uniform float in [0, 1)
float NextFloat();
float Range(float lo, float hi);
/// True with probability p
bool Chance(float p);
/// A uniform point inside the unit sphere, and a uniform unit direction
Vec3 InUnitSphere();
Vec3 OnUnitSphere();
```

### shard/cpp/reflect.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : what exists in the engine and in the plugins, described at run time ; and functions to be called by name (`shard_reflect.h`).

```cpp
// a visual scripting editor lists what it can wire together
for (const auto& type : Shard::Reflect::Types(Shard::TypeKind::Component))
    for (const auto& field : type.fields) AddPin(type.name, field.name, field.type);
for (const auto& fn : Shard::Reflect::Functions()) AddNode(fn.category, fn.name, fn.params, fn.results);

// a plugin offers a function to the graphs, the UI bindings and the console
ctx.Reflect().AddFunction("nav.set_destination", "AI/Navigation", "Sends an agent to a point",
    { { "agent", ValueType::Actor }, { "target", ValueType::Vec3 } }, { { "ok", ValueType::Bool } },
    [](const std::vector<Shard::Value>& in, std::vector<Shard::Value>& out) { out[0] = Shard::Value(Navigate(in[0].AsActor(), in[1].AsVec3())); return true; });

auto out = Shard::Reflect::Call("math.add", { Shard::Value(1.f), Shard::Value(2.f) });         // std::optional<std::vector<Value>>
```

### shard/cpp/registry.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : registrations that live where the code lives.

A plugin of one file registers everything in OnLoad. A game does not: each .cpp defines its own scripts, components and systems and says so at the bottom of the file, with one of these macros. They add themselves to a list when the library is loaded, and the SDK runs the list at the start of OnLoad, in a fixed order (by kind, then by name - never by the order the compiler happened to link the files, which would change the ids of the components and the order of the systems from one build to the next).

```cpp
SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Health, (maxHealth)(current))                   // shard/cpp/script.hpp
SHARD_DEFINE_COMPONENT(Velocity, (x)(y)(z))                           // a component of plain data, found anywhere with Shard::ComponentOf<Velocity>()
SHARD_ON_LOAD(Movement, ctx) { ctx.Systems().Add(...).Run(...); }     // anything else: systems, cvars, commands, hooks, events...
```

The macros go at global scope, in a source file of the plugin's library (not in a static library the plugin links: the linker may drop a file nothing references).

```cpp
/// The body that follows runs in OnLoad, after the components and the scripts are registered: `ctx` is the Shard::Context. `Name` only orders
/// and names it (unique in the plugin, letters and digits).
SHARD_ON_LOAD(Name, ctx)
```

### shard/cpp/render.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : what a plugin puts on the screen (`shard_render.h`) : meshes it builds, textures it fills, sprites, instances and a 2D overlay.

```cpp
// voxels : a chunk is a mesh and an object
Shard::MeshBuilder b(SHARD_VERTEX_POSITION | SHARD_VERTEX_NORMAL | SHARD_VERTEX_UV0);
b.Quad(corner0, corner1, corner2, corner3, normal);
Shard::Mesh mesh = Shard::Mesh::Create(b);                       // from a job if you like : creating records, the GPU work happens later
Shard::RenderObject chunk = Shard::RenderObject::Create(mesh, { &material }, { chunkOrigin });

// particles : a batch of sprites, set again every frame
Shard::SpriteBatchOptions o; o.texture = &tex; o.blend = SHARD_BLEND_ALPHA; o.maxSprites = 4096;
Shard::SpriteBatch smoke = Shard::SpriteBatch::Create(o);
smoke.Set(sprites);

// a UI : an overlay draws into the frame
Shard::Overlay ui = Shard::Overlay::Add("ui", 0, [&](const Shard::OverlayFrame& f, Shard::Canvas& c) { c.DrawGeometry(g, &atlas, { 10.f, 10.f }); });
```

Every class owns its handle (move only) : the resource goes when the object does, and the host releases whatever is left with the plugin.

### shard/cpp/script.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : scripts, the gameplay classes of a game (`shard_scripts.h`).

```cpp
// health.hpp
class Health : public Shard::Script {
public:
    float maxHealth = 100.f;                    // fields: shown in the inspector, saved with the world
    float current = 100.f;
    Shard::Text label;

    void OnPlay() override { current = maxHealth; }
    void OnTick(float dt) override { if (current <= 0.f) Owner().Destroy(); }
    void Damage(float amount) { current -= amount; }
};

// health.cpp
#include "health.hpp"
SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Health, (maxHealth)(current)(label))
```

Put as many scripts as you like in as many files as you like: each registers itself (`shard/cpp/registry.hpp`). In the editor the script is a component, `"<plugin id>.Health"`, that you add to an actor like any other: its object is created with the component, its callbacks run in play mode in the same order as the engine's own scripts (the order the components were added), and it goes with the actor.

The class is a normal C++ class: any member that is not listed stays out of the inspector and the world file, and starts fresh (a copy of the actor for play mode builds a new object and copies the listed fields into it). Keep the constructor free of calls into the engine (the SDK builds one to learn where the fields are): do that work in OnCreate or OnPlay.

#### `Contact`

A contact of the actor's body with another one (physics). The actor needs a `"physics_body"` component.

```cpp
/// the other body's actor
Actor other;
/// points from this actor toward the other one
Vec3 normal;
/// a point of the contact, in the world
Vec3 point;
/// how deep the bodies overlap
float penetration = 0.f;
```

#### `Script`

The base of a gameplay class. Override what you need; the host calls them as it calls the engine's own scripts.

```cpp
/// The script joined an actor that is in a world (a component added in play mode, a world loaded, a spawn)
virtual void OnCreate();
/// The world finished loading
virtual void OnWorldLoaded();
virtual void OnWorldUnloaded();
/// Play mode starts (the first thing a script of the world does)
virtual void OnPlay();
/// Every frame; `deltaTime` is the frame's, in seconds
virtual void OnTick(float /*deltaTime*/);
/// Every fixed simulation step, right before the physics step: forces and anything that must be reproducible go here
virtual void OnFixedTick(float /*fixedDeltaTime*/);
/// Every frame, after the scripts and the physics moved everything: cameras and whatever follows what moved
virtual void OnLateTick(float /*deltaTime*/);
/// Play mode stops
virtual void OnStop();
/// The script or its actor is destroyed
virtual void OnDestroyed();
virtual void OnActivated();
virtual void OnDeactivated();
/// The physics step found this actor's body touching another one, still touching it, or no longer touching it (OnContactEnded only
/// knows `other`). They run right after the step, so the bodies can be read and changed.
virtual void OnContactAdded(const Contact&);
virtual void OnContactPersisted(const Contact&);
virtual void OnContactEnded(const Contact&);
/// Every frame the world does NOT play (the editor's edit mode), with the real frame time : a particle emitter, a UI being laid out, a preview.
/// Only for a class that declares `static constexpr bool kExecuteInEditMode = true;`. What it does must not change what gets saved.
virtual void OnEditTick(float /*deltaTime*/);
/// The inspector (or an undo, or SetComponentJson) edited a field : its index among the fields the class registered, in the order of the
/// registration (Shard::FieldIndex<T>("name") finds an index by name). Not called for what the script changes itself.
virtual void OnFieldChanged(uint32_t /*fieldIndex*/);
/// The actor this script is on
const Actor& Owner() const;
/// The world it is in
Scene GetScene() const;
```

```cpp
/// The index of the field `name` of the script class T (what OnFieldChanged is told), or -1
```

```cpp
/// Registers a script class under its class name. At global scope, in a source file of the plugin (it needs <shard/game.hpp>).
/// The fields are the members the class declares with SHARD_FIELD (shard/cpp/field.hpp), each with its own options, in the header :
/// SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Health)
/// The older way lists the members here instead (any field type of shard/cpp/component.hpp : numbers, bool, Vec2/3/4, Quat, Color, Text, AssetId,
/// Blob), and the two may be mixed :
/// SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Health, (maxHealth)(current))
/// SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT_EX adds the options of the listed fields (Shard::FieldOptions: bounds, tooltip, SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME), in parentheses:
/// SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT_EX(Health, (maxHealth)(current), ({ "maxHealth", 0, 0.f, 1000.f, "hit points" }))
SHARD_DETAIL_UNPAREN(...)
/// A script whose fields are declared in the class (SHARD_FIELD), or with no fields at all (it only reacts : OnTick, contacts...)
SHARD_DETAIL_SCRIPT_DECLARED(Class)
template <typename T> ComponentType<T>& ComponentOf();
```

### shard/cpp/time.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : the simulation's clock and a fingerprint of its state (`shard_time.h`).

```cpp
const auto t = Shard::Time::Now();
Send(Message{ t.fixedStep, ... });                    // a tick number two peers agree on
if (t.fixedStep % 60 == 0) Send(Shard::Time::Hash()); // compare it with the other peer's to know they stayed in step
```

`simTime` and `fixedStep` are the simulation's (a replay reproduces them) ; `realTime` is the machine's, for what is not part of the game.

#### `TimeInfo`

### shard/cpp/worlds.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : loading worlds (`shard_worlds.h`). Prefabs are spawned with `Scene::SpawnPrefab`.

```cpp
if (reachedExit) Shard::Worlds::Load("worlds/level2.world");
```

The load is a request : the engine swaps the worlds at the start of a later frame, so the script that asks keeps running until then.

#### `Worlds`

```cpp
/// Asks for the world at that path of the project to replace the loaded ones. False : the project has no such world, or a load is already
/// under way.
static bool Load(std::string_view pathInProject);
/// True while a requested load is under way
static bool IsLoading();
static int LoadedCount();
/// The loaded world at an index (0 .. LoadedCount() - 1), if there is one
static std::optional<Loaded> At(int index);
```
